title: TAPPaaS Positions
description: config/positions.json — the site's physical assets and where they are inside its locations: the rooms (each in a location of site.json), the racks, every placement, the assets (with their ports and lifecycle, ADR-040 D7-D9), the cables nothing can see, and the faceplates the site adds to the catalog. Site state, written only by asset-manager. A placement and a cable end name a device as the physical topology does (a node, a switch, an access point, a machine, an asset's role) or an asset with no role by its own name; the device's own record is never touched. A cable between two devices the switches or LLDP already see is not recorded here: the topology draws it. An absent file is an empty one. assets{} is interim: ADR-040 step 3 moves it into the CMDB, its shape the CMDB's asset and port classes'.

placements.description: Where each device stands, keyed by the name the topology knows it by (an asset's role while it plays one, else the asset's own name): in a rack at its units, or loose in a room (no rack, no unit); a disk in a bay of another asset (in, bay). A device has at most one placement. A passive device nothing records (a PDU) by its own name.

cables.description: Cables nothing can see: the ISP hand-off, a patch panel, a PDU; and the segments of a link split at a patch panel. A port carries at most one cable, a patch panel's port one on its front and one on its rear.

assets.description: The physical assets, keyed by name (a tag per kind — srv-01, sw-01, ap-01, dev-01 — or the operator's own): each with its kind, its records (vendor, model, serial, asset tag, procurement, disposal), its ports, its lifecycle stage, a faulty flag, and the role it plays — the topology's name for the node, switch, access point or device it is allocated to (ADR-040 D7). One that plays no node, switch or AP is a device of the topology, by its role's name or its own: placeable and a cable end.

rooms.description: The rooms, keyed by name: where racks stand and devices stand loose. Each is in a location of site.json.

faceplates.description: The site's own faceplates, keyed <vendor>/<model>: plates for models the shipped catalog lacks, merged over it. An entry of a shipped key replaces the shipped plate (validate says so).

name.description: The rack's name: lower case, digits and dashes. It is the record's key.
name.changeNote: The placements name the rack: add a rack under the new name, move the devices, delete the old one.

displayName.description: The name shown on the rack's frame.

units.description: The rack's height in rack units (U).
units.changeNote: Refused while a device would no longer fit.

width.description: The rack's width: a 19-inch rack, or a 10-inch one.

numbering.description: How the rack's units are numbered: U1 at the bottom (bottom-up), or at the top (top-down).
numbering.changeNote: Renumbers every device's position as drawn; the recorded U of each placement stays.

room.description: The room the rack stands in: a room record's name (asset-manager room add). Text naming no room yet is kept as it is, with a note.

description.description: What the rack is for, in a line.

device.description: The placed device: its name in the physical topology. It is the record's key.
device.changeNote: A placement is one device's: unplace it and place the other device.

in.description: A disk's: the asset it is in, by the asset's own name (a server, never a disk). A disk is placed only so; nothing else is.
in.changeNote: place <disk> --in <asset> moves it: its CMDB record in the old asset ends, one in the new begins.

bay.description: A disk's: the bay of that asset it is in, as the asset labels it, else the disk's by-id name.

rack.description: The rack it is mounted in. A device loose in a room has none.

u.description: The lowest rack unit it occupies, as the rack numbers its units. A device loose in a room has none.

room.description: For a device in no rack: the room it stands loose in. A device in a rack is in its rack's room.

height.description: In a rack: how many rack units it occupies.

width.description: In a rack: how much of its width it takes, all of it, a half or a third.

slot.description: For a half- or third-width device: its column, 0 at the left.

face.description: In a rack: the side it faces.

faceplate.description: The faceplate drawn for it, from the catalog (vendor/model). Unset: the catalog's suggestion for the device's model, else a generic plate.

label.description: The label on the device, drawn on its plate.

description.description: A note on where it stands.

device.description: A device of the topology, an asset (by its role, else its own name), a placed device, or one this cable places (with its faceplate).

port.description: The port, as the device's faceplate or the topology names it.

faceplate.description: For a device only this cable places (the ISP's modem): its faceplate.

side.description: On a patch panel's port: its front (the default) or its rear.

from.changeNote: Remove the cable and add it again.

to.changeNote: Remove the cable and add it again.

origin.description: A segment of a link split at a patch panel (cable split): what the link was — one the topology sees, or a recorded cable that cable join records again.

linkSpeed.description: The link speed seen on the cable (ADR-040 D9): the connection's, where a port's speed is its maximum — a 10G cage holding a 1G module shows 1g here. A number and its unit, lowercase.

name.description: The port's name: the label on the case, or the OS's name (enp97s0). Unique on its asset; no colon.
name.changeNote: A cable names the port: remove the port and add it under the new name.

kind.description: The connector (ADR-040 D9): what one plugs a cable into. A BMC is an rj45 port with role bmc; power, video and serial are no ports.

speed.description: The port's maximum: rj45 1g, 2.5g or 10g; sfp 1g, 10g or 25g; usb-a and usb-c usb2 or usb3. The link it negotiates is the cable's linkSpeed.

standard.description: A wifi port's standard (Wi-Fi 6E is wifi6 with band 6).

bands.description: A wifi port's bands, in GHz.

module.description: What an sfp cage holds: a direct-attach cable, a short- or long-range optic, an RJ45 module.

role.description: What the node uses it for.

mac.description: Its MAC address. Unique across every port of every asset: a reservation or a registration that names a MAC names one asset.

side.description: On a patch panel: a port on one side only. Absent: it has a front and a rear, each taking one cable.

name.description: The asset's name: a tag per kind (srv-NN, sw-NN, ap-NN, dev-NN, dsk-NN — the next free one when none is given) or the operator's own. It is the record's key and never changes; the role's name is what the views label it with.
name.changeNote: The asset's history is under its name: add a new asset for a new thing.

disk.description: A disk's own record (kind disk): its medium, bus, World Wide Name, size and firmware, beside the vendor, model and serial every asset has. Its serial is its identity: unique across the assets, compared without case, spaces and dashes.

description.description: What it is, where it comes from.

model.description: Its model: a faceplate key (vendor/model) where the catalog has one — its ports then come from the plate, its own merged over them by name — else the model's name.

serial.description: Its serial number: the key a controller or the installer reports it by. Unique across the assets.

assetTag.description: The site's own tag on the case, if it has one.

ports.description: Its ports (ADR-040 D9), merged over its model's plate's by name.

location.description: The location it is at: a location of site.json (site-manager location list). Unset: the primary location. Its placement's room must be at the same location.

stage.description: Its lifecycle stage as recorded (ADR-040 D7): ordered, stock, placed or disposed. The view derives operational (it has a role) and placed (it has a placement); the verbs keep this in step. An ordered or disposed asset has no placement and no role.
stage.changeNote: asset receive, place, unplace, asset dispose.

faulty.description: A flag beside the stage: it is faulty (a failed fan, a dead port, away for repair). asset fault sets it with a note, asset repaired clears both.

faultNote.description: What is wrong, when it is faulty.

procurement.description: How it was bought (optional). No prices.

ownership.description: Owned, or rented (a rented dedicated server).

disposal.description: How it left (asset dispose): only on a disposed asset, whose record stays.

wiped.description: For an asset with disks: whether they were wiped.

role.description: The role it plays for the time being: the topology's name for the node, machine, switch or access point it is allocated to, or for the device nothing manages that it is (asset allocate, asset release). Placements and cables name the role while it has one. Unset: it plays none.
role.changeNote: asset allocate and asset release; a placement and cables move to the asset's own name when the role ends.

name.description: The room's name: how racks and placements name it. It is the record's key.
name.changeNote: Racks and placements name it: add the new room, move them, delete this one.

location.description: The location the room is in: a location of site.json (site-manager location list). Unset: the primary location.
location.changeNote: Refused while a device placed in the room records another location of its own.

width.description: Its share of the rack's width. Unset: full.

ports.description: Its ports as a port spec: groups side by side (a comma between), rows within a group (a slash between), items within a row (a plus between), each [<n>x]<kind>[-<speed>][@<rows>][:<name>]; a speed (1g, 2.5g, 10g, 25g) is the port's maximum, one its connector comes in (absent: rj45 and poe 1g, sfp+ 10g, sfp28 25g); a group may end in its place in percent of the plate's width, [<from>-<to>]. 24xrj45 · 8xrj45, 2xsfp+ · 8xsfp+/8xsfp+ · 8xrj45-2.5g.

passive.description: Nothing sees it (a patch panel, a PDU): placed without a topology device.

match.description: The models and names an inventory reports it by: the plate is suggested for them.

vendor.description: The vendor as drawn. Unset: the key's.

displayName.description: The model as drawn. Unset: the key's.
